title: CombatState
description: The root of `combat-state.json`: the battle as the player's HUD shows it, written when every phase begins and after every unit's activation; the file exists only while a battle is running.

modVersion.description: The four-part version of the mod that wrote the file; the other files match the catalog written by the same version.

exportedAt.description: When the file was last written, in ISO 8601 with the local time's UTC offset.

trigger.description: What caused the export that last wrote the file.

contract.description: The contract being fought, as in mission-outcome.json contract.

mapId.description: The battle's map, as combat-map.json mapId.

phase.description: The current phase as the HUD numbers it, as CombatUnitState.initiative: units act from 5 down to 1.

resolve.description: The lance's resolve now; its limits are in rules.json combat.resolve.

units.description: Every unit the player knows of, keyed by the game's unit id: the player's and allied units, and the enemies and neutral units the HUD shows or last showed. A destroyed unit stays, as its wreck is on the map; an enemy or neutral unit that withdrew or that the mission's script removed leaves no wreck and is left out.

objectives.description: The objectives the HUD lists, finished ones included, in the HUD's order.

zones.description: The zones drawn on the map.

landingZones.description: Where a dropship or drop pods are about to land; entries come and go as the mission readies landings and they happen. The game ties none to the objective announcing it: match them by hex with the objective's `beacon`. A lance arriving without drop pods or a dropship has none; the band along the encounter boundary, which the HUD marks the same way, isn't exported.

buildingSides.description: The buildings on a side, e.g. a base to destroy or defend, by their combat-map.json buildings[].id, in the order of their ids; the others are on none. The mission's script can change a building's side during the battle.

damagedBuildings.description: The buildings below their max structure, destroyed ones included, by their combat-map.json buildings[].id, in the order of their ids; the others are undamaged.

oneOf.description: A career is loaded, new or from a save. The game state is skipped while a finished contract's results are still to be applied, and the catalog is rebuilt only when it's missing or stale, once the game has loaded every vehicle, turret and design mask.
The player saves the career outside combat.
The game saves the career on its own outside combat, e.g. once an event's popup is closed with the picked option's results applied, or once a contract's results are applied.
A contract's results are applied, salvage included, where the game doesn't save the career afterwards, which is `autosave` otherwise.
The monthly financial report is shown, with the expenses paid.
A mech lab order completes, at the end of a day or right away when it has nothing left to do; when several work orders complete together, the last one names the export.
A pilot's healing in the med bay completes, as `mechLabOrderCompleted`.
An Argo upgrade's installation completes, as `mechLabOrderCompleted`.
The game has generated a star system's contracts.
The ship has jumped into its destination star system, once the game has refreshed the star system's stores and hiring hall, with its contracts; work orders completing that day export with it.
The ship arrives at the planet after a trip.
A store closes, from the main screen or the mech lab.
The store screen completes a purchase, or refuses one.
The store screen completes a sale, or refuses one, once for a stack sold at once.

The mech bay changes: a refit, repair, readying or storing is queued, an order is cancelled, the work queue is reordered, a mech or chassis is stored or scrapped, a stored component's repair is queued, or a mech is renamed without a refit.
The barracks confirm a pilot's training.
The game asks where to put a new mech because every mech bay is full, e.g. after salvage completes one.
A mission ends, still in combat, before the salvage is chosen.
The after-action report has finalized the salvage: once the priority salvage is confirmed, or right away when there is nothing to choose.
An Argo upgrade is bought and its installation starts.
A phase begins, before its first unit acts: the battle's first once the lance is deployed, and every later one, also one reached by reserving units.
A new battle begins, when the briefing is dismissed.
A battle is loaded from a save, continuing mid-phase.
A unit's activation is done, its attacks resolved; out of contact, once the player's units have all moved. Reserving a unit doesn't count.

MissionContract.description: The contract a mission was for.

id.description: The contract's id from the game's data files; `null` when the game keeps no reference to it.

name.description: The contract's name, as the contract list shows it.

type.description: The mission type, described in rules.json contractTypes.

displayStyle.description: Whether it's a regular, story, restoration or flashpoint contract.

employer.description: The faction that hires the company.

target.description: The faction the mission is fought against; `INVALID_UNSET`, which has no catalog.json factionDefinitions entry, for a story contract that only travels.

difficulty.description: The difficulty on the skulls' scale of 1 to 10 (two per skull), capped at rules.json campaign.contracts.maxGlobalDifficulty and limited by rules.json reputationLevels[].maxContractDifficulty.

starSystem.description: The star system the mission is fought in.

DefinitionReference.description: A game definition: its id from the game's data files and the name shown in the UI.

id.description: The definition's id from the game's data files, or its name in the game's enumeration where it has no data file (e.g. the player's faction).

ContractDisplayStyle.description: Whether a contract is a regular, story, restoration or flashpoint contract.

CombatUnit.description: A unit in combat, with as much of it as the HUD shows at its visibility.

side.description: Whose side the unit is on.

visibility.description: How much of the unit the HUD shows, deciding which of its other fields are set.

kind.description: The kind of unit; `null` when the HUD doesn't tell: at `blipMinimum` and `lastSeen`.

tonnage.description: The unit's tonnage, in tons; `null` when the HUD doesn't tell: for a blip below `blipMaximum`, a turret blip, which shows its weight class instead, and when last seen.

weightClass.description: The unit's weight class; `null` when the HUD doesn't tell: for a blip below `blipMaximum`, a mech or vehicle blip, which shows its tonnage instead, and when last seen.

definition.description: The mech, vehicle or turret in the catalog, which holds its armor and loadout; `null` when the unit is out of full view or one of the player's mechs, which have bayMech instead.

bayMech.description: The player's mech in `game-state.json`, whose loadout holds its assigned armor; `null` when the unit isn't one.

hex.description: The hex the unit stands on, or was last detected on for `lastSeen`; a unit stands on its center.

elevation.description: The height in meters the unit is at, or was last detected at, to 0.1 m, on the scale of the elevations in combat-map.json hexes.

facingDegrees.description: The direction the unit faces, in degrees clockwise seen from above, to 0.1°: 0 towards the map's +z, 90 towards its +x, as in combat-map.json hexGrid.centerFormula, up to below 360. A blip's marker shows it at every level; `null` when last seen.

terrain.description: The terrain the unit stands in, keyed as in catalog.json terrainDefinitions, which a blip's position on the map shows; `null` when on open ground or last seen.

pilot.description: The pilot, which the HUD names only in full view (`full`); `null` when the unit is out of full view or has no pilot.

state.description: The unit's condition, which the HUD shows only in full view (`full`); `null` when the unit is out of full view.

linesOfFire.description: The lines of fire to the units it could attack: from the player's units to every living enemy in full view (`full`), and from those enemies to the player's units, in the order of the targets' unit ids. `null` when the unit is destroyed or neither of those. The hit chance isn't exported: it follows from rules.json combat.toHit and changes as soon as a unit moves.

movement.description: Where the player's unit can move and what it gets there; `null` when the unit isn't the player's or can't move (a turret, a prone or shut down mech).

TeamSide.description: A team's side: a unit's or a building's.

allegiance.description: Whose side the team is on.

UnitAllegiance.description: Whose side a team in combat is on, seen from the player: its units' and its buildings'.

oneOf.description: The player's own lance.
A team on the player's side, e.g. the employer's units.
A team fighting the player's side.
A team neither side fights, until it turns hostile.

UnitVisibility.description: How much of a unit the player's HUD shows (the game's VisibilityLevel).

oneOf.description: In sight of the player's side, allied units' sensors included, or one of its own units: everything the HUD can show. An enemy in sight but hidden by ECM counts too, though the HUD hides its pilot, heat, stability and initiative. A destroyed unit stays in full view.
A sensor blip with the unit's kind and tonnage, or a turret's weight class.
A sensor blip with the unit's kind.
A sensor blip with nothing but its position.
Out of sensor range, where the player's side last detected it; not known to be destroyed.

UnitKind.description: The kind of a unit in combat, which tells the catalog group of its definition.

oneOf.description: A mech, the player's, an ally's or an enemy's.
A ground unit with fixed armor and loadout.
A fixed emplacement with a single location.

MechReference.description: A mech in the mech bay, by its own id and name there (game-state.json mechs).

id.description: The game's own id of the mech in the mech bay.

HexCoordinates.description: A hex of the game's movement grid by its axial coordinates, as in combat-map.json hexes.

q.description: The hex's axial `q`, as in combat-map.json hexGrid.

r.description: The hex's axial `r`, as in combat-map.json hexGrid.

PilotReference.description: A pilot: their id, full name without callsign, and callsign.

name.description: The pilot's full name without callsign.

callsign.description: The pilot's callsign, which isn't part of name.

CombatUnitState.description: A unit's condition as the HUD shows it, for a unit in full view.

deathMethod.description: How the unit was destroyed (the game's DeathMethod), e.g. `LegDestruction`, a turret's `CenterTorsoDestruction`, a vehicle's `VehicleLocationDestroyed`, or `PilotKilled` also for an incapacitated pilot; `null` when the unit lives.

locations.description: The armor and structure left per location, in the game's order: a mech's from head to legs, a vehicle's from front to rear and turret, a turret's single one. The limits are in CombatUnit.definition or CombatUnit.bayMech.

evasionPips.description: The evasion pips the unit has, earned by moving (see rules.json combat.evasion).

guard.description: The unit's guard level and its sources.

isEntrenched.description: Whether the unit is entrenched, e.g. by bracing, until its next activation: weapons' stability damage against it is multiplied by rules.json combat.stability.entrenchedInstabilityMultiplier.

isProne.description: Whether the mech has been knocked down; only mechs can be.

isShutDown.description: Whether the unit is shut down, e.g. from overheating.

isUnsteady.description: Whether the mech is unsteady: its instability rose above MechStability.unsteadyAbove and hasn't fallen below since; only mechs can be.

mech.description: What only a mech has; `null` when the unit is a vehicle or turret.

hasActivated.description: Whether the unit has finished its activation this round.

initiative.description: The phase the unit acts in, on the scale of phase.

components.description: Every component mounted, in the game's order.

pilot.description: The pilot's condition; `null` when the unit has no pilot.

abilities.description: The pilot's and components' abilities that can be activated, with their cooldowns.

resolveCosts.description: What Precision Strike and Vigilance cost the unit now, which its pilot's spirits change; `null` when the unit isn't in the player's lance, which alone spends resolve.

DeathMethod.description: How a unit was destroyed, as the game records it.

UnitLocation.description: A location's armor and structure left, in whole points as the paper doll shows them: cut off, a remainder below 1 shown as 1.

location.description: The game's name of the location: a mech's as in catalog.json chassisDefinitions.*.locations[].location, a vehicle's as in catalog.json vehicleDefinitions.*.locations[].location, or `Structure` for a turret's single location.

armor.description: The armor left, by side; only a mech's torso has a rear.

structure.description: The structure left; 0 once the location is destroyed.

front.description: The front armor; outside the torso, the location's only armor.

rear.description: The rear armor; `null` when the location is outside the torso.

Guard.description: The unit's guard, which the HUD shows as guarded at level 1 or more.

level.description: What the sources below add up to: bracing and cover 1 each, Bulwark 1 more on top of either; Bulwark not after a melee hit since the unit's last activation. Bracing and Bulwark don't count while the guard is broken (unsteady, prone, shut down, sensor locked or hit), and none while the unit moves.

isBraced.description: Braced in its last activation, until its next one.

hasCover.description: Standing in a terrain that grants guard.

MechState.description: What only a mech's condition has: its heat and stability bars.

MechHeat.description: A mech's heat as the HUD's heat bar shows it, with the thresholds it draws and the sinking it predicts.

dissipation.description: The heat the mech sheds at the end of its activation now: its heat sinks after the terrain it stands in, the biome and effects.

overheatsAbove.description: The heat above which the mech overheats, after the pilot's Guts and effects; the base is in rules.json combat.heat.overheatsAbove.

maxHeat.description: The heat at which the mech shuts down, after heat banks and effects; the base is in rules.json combat.heat.maxHeat.

MechStability.description: A mech's stability as the HUD's stability bar shows it, with the thresholds it draws.

current.description: The instability taken, from 0 up, as the bar fills.

unsteadyAbove.description: The instability above which the mech is unsteady and loses its evasion pips, after effects; the base is rules.json combat.stability.unsteadyAbovePercent of maxStability.

maxStability.description: The instability at which the mech is knocked down: the chassis' stability, as its `MaxStability` statistic has it now.

CombatComponent.description: A component mounted on a unit, with its condition in the battle.

component.description: The component, by the id its definition is keyed by.

location.description: The game's name of the location it is mounted in, as UnitLocation.location.

damageLevel.description: The component's damage level, e.g. `Penalized` or `Destroyed`.

shotsLeft.description: The shots left in an ammunition box, or in a weapon that carries its own; `null` when it's another component. A destroyed box has none.

ComponentReference.description: A reference to a component's definition, with its type. Components are ordered by type, then by name, with the id breaking ties.

id.description: The component definition's id from the game's data files.

type.description: The game's component type, e.g. `Weapon` or `AmmunitionBox`, which names the component's group in catalog.json componentDefinitions; never `NotSet`, `Special` or `MechPart`, which the game's enum also has.

ComponentType.description: The game's kind of component, which names the component's group in catalog.json componentDefinitions.

CombatPilotState.description: A unit's pilot's condition in the battle.

injuries.description: The injuries, including those from before the mission.

health.description: The injuries at which the pilot is incapacitated, as in mission-outcome.json lance[].health.

bonusHealth.description: The bonus health left, which takes hits before they become injuries and is used up by them; the portrait shows it on top of health.

skills.description: The skill levels the game computes with now, temporary changes from effects included; exported for every pilot in full view, though the HUD shows only the player's.

Skills.description: A pilot's skill levels, each from 1 to 10.

gunnery.description: The Gunnery level, whose training table is rules.json skills.gunnery.

piloting.description: The Piloting level, whose training table is rules.json skills.piloting.

guts.description: The Guts level, whose training table is rules.json skills.guts.

tactics.description: The Tactics level, whose training table is rules.json skills.tactics.

CombatAbility.description: An ability a unit can activate, as its HUD button shows it.

ability.description: The ability, the pilot's or a mounted component's.

cooldown.description: The unit's activations until the ability can be used again; 0 when ready.

usesLeft.description: The uses left of an ability that can be used only so often; `null` when there's no limit.

ResolveCosts.description: The resolve a mech's Precision Strike and Vigilance cost.

precisionStrikeCost.description: The resolve a Precision Strike costs.

StandingLineOfFire.description: How a unit could fire at a target from where it stands, as hovering over the target shows it.

target.description: The target's unit id, a key of units.

blocking.description: How much of the line of fire itself is blocked. A target beyond every weapon's range and the unit's sensors is blocked too.

fire.description: Whether the unit's weapons could fire at the target directly, only indirectly or not at all, or it is out of their range.

isInFiringArc.description: Whether the target is in the unit's firing arc without turning.

LineOfFireBlocking.description: How much of a line of fire is blocked (the game's LineOfFireLevel).

oneOf.description: Nothing in the way: direct fire without a line of fire penalty.
The game's obstructed line: direct fire is still possible, with the penalties of rules.json combat.lineOfFire.
No direct fire; a weapon that can fire indirectly still may.

FireAvailability.description: How a unit could fire at a target from where it stands (the game's FiringPreviewManager).

oneOf.description: The line of fire isn't blocked and the target is within the longest weapon's range.
The line of fire is blocked, but the target is within an indirect fire weapon's range.
The line of fire isn't blocked, but the target is beyond the longest weapon's range.
Blocked, and no weapon can fire indirectly at it.

UnitMovement.description: Where a player's unit can end its move, read from the game's own pathing, with the evasion pips it gets and its lines of fire there; combat-map.json hexes give each hex's terrain and elevation. A unit that has activated gets those of its next activation, from where it stands. The facing after a move isn't exported, as the unit can turn at its end.

canSprint.description: Whether the unit can sprint; a legged or unsteady mech can't.

canJump.description: Whether the unit can jump: a mech with a working jump jet.

hexes.description: The hexes some move of the unit ends on, by `r`, then `q`.

ReachableHex.description: A hex a move of the unit can end on. Each move's evasion pips follow from the length of the path the unit would walk there, or a jump's straight distance, and abilities can raise them above the rules' table.

q.description: The hex's axial `q`, as in combat-map.json hexGrid.

r.description: The hex's axial `r`, as in combat-map.json hexGrid.

walk.description: The evasion pips a walk ending on the hex gives; `null` where no walk reaches it.

sprint.description: The evasion pips a sprint ending on the hex gives; `null` where no sprint reaches it or the unit can't sprint.

reverse.description: The evasion pips moving backward to the hex gives; `null` where no backward move reaches it.

jump.description: The evasion pips a jump to the hex gives, one for a jump in place; `null` where no jump reaches it or the unit can't jump.

linesOfFire.description: From the hex to each enemy in full view (`full`) the unit has a line of fire to or could fire at indirectly, in the order of their unit ids; an enemy it could do neither to from there has no entry.

MoveLineOfFire.description: How the unit could fire at a target after moving to a hex, as the HUD's move preview shows it.

target.description: The target's unit id, a key of units.

blocking.description: How much of the line of fire itself is blocked. A target beyond every weapon's range and the unit's sensors is blocked too.

fire.description: Whether the unit's weapons could fire at the target directly, only indirectly or not at all, or it is out of their range.

side.description: The side of the target an attack from the hex hits.

AttackSide.description: The side of a target an attack hits (the game's AttackDirection).

oneOf.description: The target's front.
The target's left side.
The target's right side.
The target's rear.
A prone target, which an attack hits anywhere.
A turret, which has a single location.

CombatObjective.description: An objective in the HUD's objective list.

id.description: The game's id of the objective, which ObjectiveZone.objectiveIds refer to.

title.description: The title the HUD shows, as plain text.

status.description: The objective's game status, e.g. `Active`, `Succeeded` or `Failed`.

isPrimary.description: Whether the HUD lists it as a primary objective.

progress.description: The progress line the HUD shows under the title, e.g. a count of units destroyed; `null` when it shows none.

targetUnitIds.description: The units it is about (to destroy, protect or escort), as keys of units, while they are in full view, destroyed ones included; blips are left out.

targetBuildingIds.description: The buildings it is about (to destroy or defend), by their combat-map.json buildings[].id.

beacon.description: The hex the HUD draws the objective's beacon above, e.g. where the reinforcements it announces will land; `null` when it draws none: an objective that marks its target units instead, or a finished one.

ObjectiveZone.description: A zone drawn on the map, e.g. a capture or evacuation zone.

id.description: The game's id of the zone.

type.description: The game's id of the zone's region definition, e.g. `regionDef_EvacZone`, which names what the zone is for.

hexes.description: The playable hexes whose center cell is in the zone, by `r`, then `q`, as in combat-map.json hexes: a unit standing on one is in it. The game decides per map cell, so a unit whose footprint reaches into the zone from a hex next to these can count as in it too.

isPreview.description: Drawn as a zone that becomes active later.

objectiveIds.description: The objectives the zone belongs to among objectives, as CombatObjective.id; empty where it belongs only to objectives the HUD doesn't list.

LandingZone.description: A landing zone the HUD marks as dangerous.

id.description: The game's id of the dropship, or of the lance spawner whose drop pods land there.

hexes.description: The hexes whose center cell the game marks, by `r`, then `q`, as in combat-map.json hexes; a unit standing on one is crushed. A dropship's whole footprint, or each drop pod's hex, one per unit of the lance.

LandingZoneKind.description: What is about to land on a landing zone.

oneOf.description: A dropship, which marks its whole footprint.
A lance's drop pods, one per unit, each marking the hex it lands on.

BuildingSide.description: A building on a side, highlighted in its team's color on the map.

id.description: The building's id in combat-map.json buildings.

side.description: Whose side the building is on.

DamagedBuilding.description: A building below its max structure, or destroyed.

id.description: The building's id in combat-map.json buildings.

structure.description: The structure left, which the HUD shows when the building is targeted; its max is in combat-map.json buildings[].maxStructure.

destroyedHexes.description: The hexes the building stood on, now with the ground's elevation and the rubble's terrain, since `combat-map.json` isn't rewritten when it falls; units on its roof drop to the ground. `null` when it stands. The blocked steps onto and off them still follow the roof, and the terrain a building's explosion changes around it isn't exported.

MapHex.description: A hex of combat-map.json hexes with its ground as it is now.

q.description: The hex's axial `q`, as in combat-map.json hexGrid.

r.description: The hex's axial `r`, as in combat-map.json hexGrid.

elevation.description: The height in meters a unit standing on the hex is at, a building's roof where one stands, to 0.1 m.

terrain.description: The terrain a unit standing on the hex is in, keyed as in catalog.json terrainDefinitions: the first that applies to its center cell of map boundary, impassable, destroyed building, deep water, water, the terrain of the building on it, road, the map's custom terrain, forest and rough ground; `null` when on open ground.
